sections.title: Structuring arguments
sections.content:
Key phrases for academic and formal writing:
• assert — state confidently. The author asserts that climate change is reversible.
• contend — argue or maintain. Critics contend that the policy is ineffective.
• refute — prove wrong. New evidence refutes the previous findings.
• substantiate — provide evidence for. You must substantiate your claims with data.
• implication — a likely consequence. The implications of this discovery are enormous.

sections.title: Hedging and certainty
sections.content:
Expressing different levels of certainty:
• arguably — it could be said. This is arguably the most important finding of the decade.
• tentative — not certain or fixed. These are only tentative conclusions at this stage.
• conclusive — putting an end to doubt. There is no conclusive evidence to support the theory.
• plausible — seeming reasonable. Her explanation is entirely plausible.
• misconception — a wrong belief. There is a common misconception that cold weather causes illness.

exercises.question: To prove that something is wrong is to:
exercises.explanation: Refute means to prove that a statement or theory is wrong.

exercises.question: A conclusion not yet fully confirmed is:
exercises.explanation: Tentative means not certain or fixed; provisional.

exercises.question: To provide evidence supporting a claim is to:
exercises.explanation: Substantiate means to provide evidence to support or prove the truth of something.

exercises.question: An idea that seems reasonable but isn't proven is:
Evidence that removes all doubt is:
exercises.explanation: Conclusive means serving to prove a case; decisive.

exercises.question: A widely held but incorrect belief is a:
exercises.hint: People believe it but it's wrong.
exercises.explanation: A misconception is a view or opinion that is incorrect based on faulty thinking.

exercises.question: 'Arguably' means:
exercises.explanation: Arguably means it could be argued; it is possibly the case.

exercises.question: To state something with confidence is to:
exercises.explanation: Assert means to state a fact or belief confidently and forcefully.
